subject: Lyra-8B-Lite compatibility matrix + staging pin proposal
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T16:22:00Z
Subject: Lyra-8B-Lite compatibility matrix + staging pin proposal

Team —

AsterCloud reached out with an open-source-ish release called Lyra-8B-Lite that looks promising for cost-sensitive chat workloads (they sent a model card and quantization notes). Before we greenlight serving this as a publicly routable variant, I want cross-functional alignment on a short compatibility gate + temporary pin so the variant doesn't accidentally get promoted to production while we validate.

Proposal (high-level):
- Create a staging variant alias: lyra8b-lite-v1 (staging)
- Temporary pin on serving rollout for 10 calendar days starting when we have baseline compat tests in CI
- Deliverables from each team by EOD +3 business days:
  - Engineering: compatibility matrix (ops supported, quantization paths, KV-cache behavior), perf estimate (p50/p95 on n1-standard and gpu pools), and required infra tests
  - Research/Quality: eval results on our core prompt set (regressions, hallucination metrics) and recommended tolerances
  - Product/PM: customer impact assessment and suggested canary policy (traffic %, fallback map)
  - Legal/Security (looping later): anything in the model card that needs redlines (data provenance, license)

Attachments AsterCloud sent: lyra8b-model-card.pdf, lyra8b-quant-notes.txt. I attached them to the Drive link above for everyone's access.

Questions for quick alignment:
1) Is a 10-day temporary pin too long? Shorter window?
2) Are there any known blockers for running the quantized build on our current kernel matrix?
3) Who will own the canary rollback runbook?

I want to avoid last-minute surprises (e.g., a model variant getting auto-promoted) — if we can lock the variant while we run the CI + eval sweep, that should be sufficient.

Assigning preliminary owners: Dev (compat matrix + infra tests), Vivek (eval suite + quality thresholds), Laura (SLA/ops sign-off), Aditya (product/customer impact / rollout plan).

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Product Lead, Serving & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-13T19:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Lyra-8B-Lite compatibility matrix + staging pin proposal

Thanks Priya — quick technical readout after a first pass:

Summary:
- Lyra-8B-Lite appears to rely on standard transformer layers but uses a custom fused attention op in their latest checkpoint. The open weights are compatible with our loader, but the fused op falls back to slower kernels unless we run a small custom kernel or rely on their PyTorch fallback.
- Quantization path: AsterCloud's suggested 8-bit PTQ (gptq-like) works but requires per-channel scales and a KV-cache rewrite for attention keys/values. That adds ~10–12% memory overhead during generation compared to our baseline 8-bit variants.
- Expected perf on our Dedicated 1xA100 baseline: p50 token latency ~28ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) with batching 1. p95 ~72ms. These are preliminary, need CI runs.

Open engineering tasks (I can own):
1) Compatibility checklist (attached: compatibility-checklist.csv) — ops coverage, dtype paths, kernel fallbacks, and required CI matrices.
2) Small kernel prototype to avoid fallback (2–3 days) — opt-in during staging.
3) KV-cache test harness update — ensures we don't regress stream generation.

Pin suggestion: I think 10 calendar days is fine if we start when the CI matrix completes. If we only need to run automated checks + eval sweep, we could tighten to 5 business days. Longer pins make scheduling harder for other model rollouts.

I'll kick off the CI matrix tonight against our staging infra and will upload perf artifacts to the Jira ticket INF-2987.

Attachments: compatibility-checklist.csv (compat matrix draft).

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T02:11:00Z
Subject: Re: Lyra-8B-Lite compatibility matrix + staging pin proposal

+1 to Dev's technical notes. A few research/quality items to call out:

Evaluation plan (I can lead):
- Held-out prompt set: our customer-facing chat prompts (1k prompts) + targeted safety probes (200 prompts)
- Metrics: exact match where applicable, response fluency, factuality proxy (entity hallucination rate), safety flag rate
- Regression tolerance: we should allow up to 3% delta in fluency but no more than 1% increase in safety flags compared to our current 7B baseline.

Staging / rollout suggestions:
- Canary: 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 48h steps with automated rollback on quality-trend regression or token-cost explosion ( >1.5x baseline).
- Telemetry: ensure token-level cost, avg confidence for hallucination detector, and per-customer regression alerts. We need explicit tracing hooks in the serving runtime (Dev, can you confirm trace points for prompt hash + variant id?).

Data/Privacy: If the model card indicates third-party licensed pretraining, legal should review. No obvious red flags in the model card but we should verify license text.

I will run the eval harness once Dev's CI artifacts are available and post a summary in INF-2987.

— Vivek
Applied ML, Inference Optimizations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick flag. Attaching the model card and our suggested PTQ guide (we used a gptq-ish pipeline with per-channel scales) — both are attached: lyra8b-model-card.pdf, lyra8b-quant-notes.txt. A few notes for your engineers:

- The model was trained on a mixture of public corpora. We include provenance in the model card.
- License: MIT-like with attribution; not copyleft.

If you want, we can schedule a short call with our infra engineer next week to walk the kernel/quant path.

1) Engineering (Dev) — complete compatibility-checklist.csv and CI perf run, upload artifacts to INF-2987 by 2027-05-17 EOD. Confirm whether kernel prototype will be needed for canary.
2) Research/Quality (Vivek) — run eval harness on the artifacts, produce report with pass/fail vs tolerances by 2027-05-18 noon.
3) Ops/SLA sign-off (Laura) — confirm we can enforce a 1% -> 5% -> 20% canary and sign off on rollback SLO by 2027-05-18 EOD.
4) Product (Aditya) — customer impact + suggested fallback map; prepare messaging and docs for release notes by 2027-05-18 EOD.

Pin decision: we'll place a temporary pin on variant promotion starting when Dev signals CI completion. I agree with a tighter window — target pin = 5 business days from CI completion unless we need extra time. Laura, please confirm if that is operationally acceptable.

Priya
